input: Plan a three-course dinner from a new cookbook

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of guests and their relationships (e.g., romantic dinner vs. family gathering vs. dinner party) changes portion sizes, formality, and how ambitious the menu should be.
Dietary restrictions or allergies among guests are hard limits that immediately eliminate entire recipe categories from consideration.
Knowing which cookbook is being used determines what cuisines, techniques, and ingredients are even on the table.
The date and occasion (e.g., casual weeknight, special celebration) sets the required level of effort and how much advance prep time is available.
The cook's confidence level and kitchen equipment affect which recipes are realistic to attempt from an unfamiliar book.
Flavour preferences or cuisine styles to emphasise (or avoid) will guide which of the cookbook's recipes are shortlisted for each course.
Understanding what 'done well' means — impressing guests, successfully learning new techniques, staying on budget — determines how to prioritise trade-offs when choosing dishes.

gold.taskTitle: Plan a three-course dinner from a new cookbook
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to select and prepare a complete three-course dinner (starter, main, dessert) using recipes from a cookbook they have not cooked from before.

questions.title: How many people are you cooking this dinner for?
questions.description: Establishes guest count, which affects portioning, shopping quantities, and overall scale of the meal.

questions.title: Which cookbook will you be cooking from?
questions.description: Identifies the specific cookbook so that the cuisine style, recipe range, and available dishes are known.

questions.title: Do any guests have dietary restrictions or allergies?
questions.description: Surfaces hard limits that rule out entire categories of recipes before any selection begins.

questions.title: When is the dinner, and what is the occasion?
questions.description: Sets the timeline for prep and determines the required formality and ambition level of the menu.

questions.title: How confident are you in the kitchen right now?
questions.description: Gauges cooking skill level so that recipe difficulty is matched to what the cook can realistically execute from an unfamiliar book.

questions.title: Are there any cuisines or flavours you want to highlight?
questions.description: Captures taste preferences and cuisine directions to guide which recipes across the three courses are shortlisted.

questions.title: What would make this dinner feel like a success to you?
questions.description: Clarifies the primary goal — impressing guests, mastering new techniques, keeping costs down, etc. — so trade-offs between dishes can be made deliberately.
